data.description:
## Summary

`rapt-dreadable-dromedary` (`aefe-614a-2631-4117`) put
`rebar._store.store_usability.store_is_usable` on the library/MCP read chokepoint
(`_reads._tracker`). The predicate spawns `git -C <tracker> rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` on
EVERY read.

The approved plan reasoned this was negligible because "the read path ALREADY spawns git
(throttled `git fetch`/reconverge via `_fresh`)". That reasoning is not quite right: `_fresh`
is throttled to at most once per minute, so on the great majority of reads there is NO git
spawn today. The predicate adds an UNTHROTTLED one.

## Measurement (this worktree, off `origin/main` 565e1856)

A 25-ticket store, `REBAR_NO_SYNC=1`, 40 iterations, predicate neutralized by monkeypatching
`store_usability.store_is_usable` to a constant (so only the probe is removed, not the guard):

```
list_tickets WITH predicate:    22.7 ms
list_tickets WITHOUT predicate:  5.6 ms
predicate overhead:             17.1 ms  (305%)
```

So on a small store the probe costs roughly 4x the read itself. In absolute terms it is one
git process startup (~17ms on this host). On the production tracker, log reduction dominates
and the relative cost is small; the 4x is a relative figure on an already-fast operation.

## Why it was not addressed in the parent change

The parent change shipped the operator-approved, plan-review-certified design unchanged. The
two obvious optimizations both have real downsides that need a deliberate decision rather than
an in-flight one:

- **Caching the verdict.** A cached "usable" answer is precisely the staleness hazard the
  parent bug is about: a store that becomes unusable mid-session would keep reading as usable.
  Any cache needs an explicit invalidation story.
- **Resolving HEAD in-process.** Reading `.git/HEAD` and following the ref by hand
  reimplements git ref resolution (packed-refs, `.git`-as-a-file for worktrees/submodules,
  detached HEAD), which is fragile — and the parent change deliberately chose the
  `footprint._git` prior-art pattern over that.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded (in this ticket) on whether the ~17ms per-read probe is accepted
      as-is, or is to be reduced, and by which mechanism.
- [ ] If reduced: the same measurement harness shows the overhead drop, AND the regression
      tests in `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py` still pass unchanged — the
      broken/no-`.git`/mid-clone cases must still raise `store_uninitialized`.
- [ ] If reduced by caching: a test proves a store that becomes unusable DURING a session is
      detected, not served from a stale "usable" verdict.
- [ ] If accepted as-is: the reasoning is recorded on `store_usability.py` so the next reader
      does not re-litigate it.
data.title: store_is_usable adds an unthrottled git spawn to every read (~17ms, 4x on a small store)
